title: Tenali and the King's Portrait with One Eye
summary: Following the historical battle of Raichur, King Krishnadevaraya carried a glorious battle scar: an enemy arrow had grazed his left cheek...
keywords: tenali and the king's portrait with one eye
full_text:
Following the historical battle of Raichur, King Krishnadevaraya carried a glorious battle scar: an enemy arrow had grazed his left cheek, leaving him partially blind in that eye. While the Emperor was proud of his martial courage, the court flatterers and nervous portrait artists struggled with how to paint his imperial likeness.

One courtier suggested covering the King's left eye with an embroidered silk patch like a pirate; another suggested painting him only from behind!
The King was disgusted by their cowardice:
'Am I a monster to be hidden? Or an emperor to be painted with truth?'

Tenali Raman stepped forward with a fresh wooden board and charcoal:
'Maharaj, your scars are the medals of our empire's freedom. An artist must paint not merely a face, but the soul of a warrior.'

Tenali requested the King to take up his golden recurve hunting bow and pose upon the palace terrace overlooking the distant blue hills.
Tenali painted for five days with natural earth pigments, lapis lazuli, and gold leaf.

When the canvas was unveiled, the entire assembly was awestruck.
Tenali had depicted King Krishnadevaraya standing upon a mountain crest at sunrise, drawing his golden bowstring taut to his ear.
The King was shown in a majestic right-side profile: his commanding right eye was open, focused with fierce, eagle-like concentration upon a distant target in the clouds, while his scarred left eye was naturally angled away in the dynamic posture of a master marksman!

The portrait did not hide the King's wound with false flattery, nor did it insult him with clumsy exposure; it placed the monarch in his natural element as the Supreme Archer and Defender of the Realm!

King Krishnadevaraya stepped down from his throne, gazing upon the canvas with profound emotion:
'Tenali, other painters saw only a blemish on my face. Thou hast seen the warrior in my heart. This portrait shall hang in the Grand Hall of Victory for centuries!'

The King awarded Tenali a hereditary jagir of land and a diamond ring, demonstrating that true respect honors reality with noble grace.
moral: Honoring human reality with dignity and heroic grace is the highest expression of art.
